Arcane's view of the Docker host.
Backrest's repositories and their last backups.
The systems a Beszel hub monitors.
What Forgejo Actions runs, and the repositories updated last.
Frigate's latest events.
Whether gluetun's tunnel is up, and where it exits.
Miniflux's newest entries.
What was added to Jellyfin last.
The prices of the cards tcg-collector follows.
The latest release of GitHub repositories.
Stock quotes from Finnhub.

OidcFlow.description: The sign-in through the provider, from its start to its callback: a cookie the server encrypts, which holds the state, the nonce and the PKCE verifier for ten minutes. Over plain HTTP, it is `hangar-oidc`.
OidcFlow.name: __Host-hangar-oidc

Session.description: The session of the page: a cookie the server signs, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`. Over plain HTTP, where a browser keeps no `Secure` cookie, it is `hangar-session`, neither `Secure` nor `__Host-`.
Session.name: __Host-hangar-session

info.description:
Hangar's API, which its page calls. Every error is a problem, in English. Every route but those of `Auth` and
`Health` takes a `Session`.
info.title: hangar-api

post.summary: Signs in a user of `hangar.yml` by password, and sets the session's cookie. A wrong email or password is a 401, and too many of them for one email a 429.
Signs out: the session's cookie is cleared.

parameters.description: The code to exchange for the tokens.
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: The provider's error, as `access_denied` when the user declines.
parameters.name: error

parameters.description: The state the sign-in sent the provider, which must come back as it went.
parameters.name: state

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back: the session's cookie for a user `hangar.yml` lists, by its subject or its verified email, and a redirect to the page; any other is sent back to `/login` with an `error` that says why.
Starts a sign-in through the provider: a redirect to it, with the flow's cookie. A 404 when no provider is configured.
What the sign-in page offers.
The signed-in user. A session past a day is renewed for seven more, so that one in use does not expire.
The file as it is written.

put.summary: Checks the file, then writes it as it is and links the apps and shared files it lists. A file that is not valid is a 400 that names the field at fault, and is not written; a store not cloned yet is a 409.

get.summary: Every installed app, by name, with no container yet or not: one never started is stopped.
An installed app with its services and containers. A 404 for an app that is not installed.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

get.summary: The log of a container of an app, followed: its last 200 lines, then each new one, and an `end` once the container stops. A 404 for an id that is not that of a container of the app, 12 to 64 hexadecimal digits.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

get.summary: What the daemon changed, once the server's cache holds it: a page reads again what it shows. What changed before the stream opened is not in it, so a page reads everything again once it is open. It does not end.
The batches that run, and the last 20 that ended in the last five minutes, by id.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

post.summary: Starts a batch, once every app is checked: a 400 for a name compose does not take, no app at all or more than are installed, a 404 for an app that is not installed, a 409 for an app another batch, an install or an uninstall holds, and none runs. Then its output, from its start: the `batch`, a `started` per app, its lines, its `finished`, and an `end` with the report. The batch goes on once the stream is closed, holding its apps until it ends; each app's end is notified.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

get.summary: The output of a batch from its start, as far as it keeps it, then as it comes, to its `end`. A 404 for a batch that is not listed.
The usage of the whole host.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

get.summary: The resource usage of the running containers of the installed apps, a frame every second. Each stream measures its CPU shares from its own samples: the first frame has none. It does not end; a daemon that fails ends it with a problem.
The variables on disk; none before the file exists.

put.summary: Merges the changes into the file as it is on disk now, so that a variable added by hand meanwhile is kept, after a copy of it aside, `.env.global.<time>.bak`; and answers the variables written. A name compose does not take, or a value with a line break, is a 400, and nothing is written.

get.summary: Answers 200 while the server serves: the healthcheck of the image.
The runs kept, the newest first: those that wait or run, and the last that ended, 50 in all.

post.summary: Cancels the run `id`: one that waits leaves its queue, one that runs stops at its next step, the end of the app it updates for the update of the apps. A 404 for a run that is not kept, a 409 for one that ended.
Runs the job of the run `id` again, in a new run that waits its turn in its queue: the run of that job that waits or runs already, when there is one. A 404 for a run that is not kept.

get.summary: The newest 30, the newest first, and the epoch of their ids.

200.description: Server-sent events, the data of each the JSON of an item, whose schema is `x-item`. A failure ends the stream with an event `problem`, whose data is a `Problem`.

get.summary: The epoch of the ids, then the notifications filed from now on, as they are, and first, given `since`, those of a greater id the server still keeps, the oldest first: a page follows the stream from the newest it holds, so that what was filed between its read of the list and the stream's opening is in it. Given an `epoch` that is not the server's, `since` counts in another and every notification kept comes first. It does not end.

post.summary: Marks notifications as shown, so that no page shows them again as toasts.

get.summary: The store's URL, whether it is cloned, and its last sync.
The store's apps, by id, those of the filters given, or all of them, and how many each filter keeps.

Location.description: Where the created resource is read, when the server says.

post.summary: Creates an app from its `compose.yml`, once `docker compose config` accepts it; a file refused creates nothing. A 409 when its id is taken, or while a sync of the store runs.

get.summary: One file of the app. A 404 when it is not there; a 400 for a path that leaves the app's folder, or a file the editor does not open: not a regular file, over 1 MiB, binary, or not UTF-8.

Location.description: Where the created resource is read, when the server says.

post.summary: Creates the file empty, and its folders. A 409 when anything is there, a hidden file included.

put.summary: Writes the file, or creates it, once checked: `docker compose config` for `compose.yml`, `docker stack config` for `compose.swarm.yml` and for `compose.yml` beside one with content, a parse for a YAML or `.env` file. A file refused is a 400 that says why, Docker's complaint included, and is left as it was. A 409 while a sync of the store runs.

get.summary: The app, and the files the editor may open. A 404 for an app the store does not carry.

post.summary: Installs an app: links it into `app-installed/`, then seeds the variables its files reference. An app installed already is left as it is. A 404 for an app the store does not carry.

Uninstalls an app: `docker compose down` first, then its link removed; its volumes and its folder in the store are kept. An app not installed is left as it is. A 404 for an app the store does not carry.

get.summary: The `compose.yml` a new app starts from.

post.summary: Clones the store, or pulls it once cloned, then links the apps `hangar.yml` lists and seeds `.env.global`, apart from the request: the sync running, which `GET /store` reads again, and notified once it ends. While one runs, the answer is that one, and no other starts. A 409 while compose batches run, which hold their apps' files.

get.summary: The widgets, in the order `hangar.yml` places them.
What the widget placed as `key` loaded. A 404 for a key the dashboard does not place, or that of a widget that loads nothing, the clock's or Docker's; a 502 when its service did not answer.

200.description: Bytes of the media type `Content-Type` says.

get.summary: An image the widget placed as `key` shows, fetched from its service: a Frigate thumbnail, a Jellyfin poster, a card of tcg-collector. Kept a day by the browser. A 404 for an id that is not letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, or that its service does not have.

tags.description:
The dashboard, as `hangar.yml` places its widgets. A widget's data is kept per placement: fresh for its `ttl`,
60 seconds unless `hangar.yml` says, then served while it reloads behind the reader for 15 minutes more, which
is also how long a service that stops answering keeps its last card. Nothing is loaded without a reader.
tags.name: Widgets
